title: Side Effects and Pure Core
definition: A side effect observes or changes state beyond a function's explicit returned result; a pure core calculates results from explicit inputs while effectful boundaries coordinate required interaction.
purpose: Make data flow testable, repeatable, and reviewable without pretending useful programs have no effects.
history: Functional programming emphasizes referential transparency; practical systems commonly isolate effects rather than eliminate them.
mental_model: Keep calculation in a transparent workshop and place console, file, clock, randomness, network, and shared-state interaction at labeled doors.
analogy: A calculator gives a result without rearranging the room; a cashier both calculates and changes inventory, but the analogy does not capture every observational effect.
common_mistakes: Calling every mutation impure even when entirely local and unobservable
Claiming useful software can eliminate all effects
Hiding time or randomness behind no-argument helpers
industry_notes: The goal is controlled, explicit effects and small boundaries, not doctrinal elimination.
ai_notes: Ask AI to inventory read effects and write effects before accepting a refactor.
interview_notes: Ask why side effects complicate tests and how to isolate them.
lab_candidates: Convert a stateful function to pure core plus boundary
